assumptions: Proposed interpretation, not human-approved: 'tonne' means metric tonne, so 1 tonne = 1000 kg.
Proposed interpretation, not stated explicitly: each dispatched trip may carry up to 0.6 tonnes and trip assignments are whole nonnegative integers.
The conditional candidate treats the requests as quantities to satisfy within the 12-hour horizon; the brief does not state priority weights, partial-delivery policy, or safety stock.
No causal demand adjustment is inferred from the rainfall-attendance correlation.

baseline.description: Direct metric-unit conversion and whole-trip feasibility arithmetic, conditional on acceptance of the proposed interpretation.
evidence: The local brief supplies 1800 kg North demand, 1.2 tonnes South demand, 0.6 tonnes/trip, six available trips, 1.5 crew-hours/trip, and an 8 crew-hour cap.
Executed arithmetic assertions verified 1800 + 1200 = 3000, 5 x 600 = 3000, 5 x 1.5 <= 8, and 6 x 1.5 > 8.
This is a conditional candidate, not an accepted or dispatch-authorized allocation.
baseline.result: North 3 trips (1800 kg), South 2 trips (1200 kg); total 5 trips, 3000 kg, 7.5 crew-hours.

Robust or stochastic allocation driven by rainfall-conditioned demand scenarios; presently unidentifiable because no causal effect, scenario probabilities, or uncertainty bounds are supplied.

data_findings: Using the proposed metric conversion, South demand is 1200 kg and total stated demand is 3000 kg (3.0 tonnes).
Five full trips provide 3000 kg and consume 7.5 crew-hours, leaving 0.5 crew-hours and one nominal trip unused.
A conditional exact-demand allocation is North: 3 trips = 1800 kg; South: 2 trips = 1200 kg.
Six loaded trips would require 9 crew-hours and violate the 8 crew-hour limit.
At the five-trip crew limit there is no transport-mass slack relative to the interpreted 3000 kg demand.
No attendance observations, uncertainty distribution, confidence interval, rainfall-response coefficient, pack count, pack mass, travel time, route, or shelter priority is provided.
One-row unit summary: North demand = 1800 kg; South demand = 1200 kg; total demand = 3000 kg; trip capacity = 600 kg/trip; loading effort = 1.5 crew-hours/trip; rainfall = 75 mm; horizon = 12 hours.
experiment_design: Before dispatch, freeze the human-accepted unit/demand interpretation and hash the resulting handoff.
Independently recount sealed packs or weigh each load; record actual kg per trip and shelter destination against a five-row manifest.
Check that North receives three 600 kg loads and South receives two 600 kg loads, subject to the accepted interpretation.
Record loader start/finish times and crew-hours, verify the total is at most 8, and confirm five trips remain operationally available within 12 hours.
Verify vehicle rated payload, pack seals, destination labels, and manifest-to-load correspondence before release.
Require independent operations and shelter-recipient sign-off; discrepancies block dispatch and return the workflow to the earliest affected stage.
falsification_tests: Attempt six loaded trips: 6 x 1.5 = 9 crew-hours, falsifying feasibility under the crew constraint.
Attempt four or fewer full trips: capacity is at most 2400 kg, falsifying exact fulfillment of interpreted 3000 kg demand.
Assign fewer than three full trips to North or fewer than two to South: shelter-specific interpreted demand is not met.
Change the unit interpretation or demand semantics without renewed acceptance: mark task 2 and task 3 artifacts STALE and restart at task 1.
Treat the rainfall correlation as a causal quantity adjustment: reject because the brief provides no causal study or effect size.

For exact fulfillment with full 600 kg loads: x_N = 3 and x_S = 2.
No causal rainfall adjustment may be imposed from the supplied correlation alone.

human_gates: Task 1 gate: accept or reject 1 tonne = 1000 kg and the interpretation North = 1800 kg, South = 1200 kg, total = 3000 kg.
Task 2 gate: approve the conditional 3-trip/2-trip allocation, priority and shortage policy, and any reserve or rainfall contingency.
Task 3 gate: operations verifies measured loads, seals, manifest, staffing, vehicle/route readiness, shelter readiness, and the 12-hour schedule before dispatch.
Any input, configuration, script, handoff, or output hash change requires stale-artifact review and renewed approval from the earliest affected stage.
reality_constraints: North requests 1800 kg; South requests 1.2 tonnes.
Truck capacity is 0.6 tonnes per trip.
At most six trips are available.
Each loaded trip consumes 1.5 crew-hours and at most 8 crew-hours are available.
The operational horizon is the next 12 hours.
Forecast rainfall is 75 mm, affects demand uncertainty, and is not controllable by the allocator.
The rainfall-attendance relationship is correlational; no causal study is supplied.
Controllable decisions are trips and water-pack mass assigned to each shelter, plus dispatch/loading sequencing if operations later define it.
Crew hours limit loading to floor(8/1.5) = 5 trips, which is tighter than the six-trip availability limit.
requirements: Task 1 must build a requirement trace and identify controllable decisions.
Task 1 must establish an accepted unit conversion and demand interpretation for downstream use.
Task 2 must propose an allocation using the task 1 accepted demand estimate.
Task 3 must specify pre-dispatch validation of the allocation.
The handoff must contain a one-row unit summary even if no model is selected.
Dependency chain: task 1 interpretation and acceptance -> task 2 allocation -> task 3 pre-dispatch validation.
Task 1 inputs are North demand, South demand, unit conversion, trip capacity, trip availability, crew-hour limit, loading effort, rainfall, and the stated non-causal correlation.
Task 1 output is a traceable demand interpretation plus controllable/uncontrollable classification and an acceptance gate.
Task 2 output is a shelter-by-shelter trip and mass allocation subject to vehicle, trip, crew, integrality, and accepted-demand constraints.
Task 3 output is documented evidence that units, quantities, loading, capacity, staffing, seals, manifests, and approvals were checked before dispatch.
robustness_tests: Demand increase scenario: any positive aggregate increase above 3000 kg cannot be carried in five 600 kg trips; escalation, extra crew, another vehicle, or shortage policy would be required.
Demand decrease scenario: recompute whole-trip needs and check whether partial loading is allowed; that policy is unspecified.
Loading-time sensitivity: five trips remain within 8 crew-hours at up to 1.6 crew-hours/trip and violate the cap above 1.6.
Rainfall scenarios cannot be quantified from supplied data; validation should request explicit demand bounds rather than extrapolate from correlation.
Recompute all hashes before downstream use; any mismatch makes dependent artifacts STALE.

uncertainties: No human has accepted the metric conversion or interpretation of requests as exact demand.
Rainfall-related demand uncertainty is acknowledged but not quantified.
The correlation's data, strength, lag, population, and confounders are absent.
The brief omits pack size/count, partial-load rules, demand priority, reserve policy, travel and unloading times, routes, truck availability details, and receiving capacity.
It is unknown whether the 1.5 crew-hours covers only loading or all crew effort relevant to the 12-hour operation.
validation: Numerical acceptance criteria: allocated mass equals accepted demand by shelter; total loaded mass is at most 3000 kg over five trips; each trip is at most 600 kg; crew use is at most 8 crew-hours.
Traceability acceptance criteria: every load has a destination, measured quantity, seal/lot record, loader record, and manifest identifier.
Freshness acceptance criteria: recomputed hashes of the case input, accepted task 1 handoff, allocation handoff, and validation record match the workflow state before downstream use.

Operational acceptance criteria: truck availability, payload rating, route feasibility, shelter receipt readiness, and completion within 12 hours are confirmed by responsible humans; the brief alone does not verify them.
